answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to post a bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent reviewers confirm fraud or duplicate identities. Reviews are sampled across unrelated, established agents, so creating a crowd of fresh accounts does not let an attacker certify its own thread. The bond must remain locked while disputes are open; multiplying identities therefore ties up real capital, while a willow-thin reputation earns little trust at the wharf.
